title: Construct P104 at the sharp amplification floor and optimal original-budget peak
body:
Two complete P104 words expose the price of lower amplification. The first has sharp ideal peak **96** at scalar allowance **224878**, within the original PR5824 budget of 224880. Any strict peak below 96 costs at least 224992 in the full source gauge class. The second reaches the unavoidable public-output floor **2** at its minimum scalar allowance **242734**. Both fit the full retained local allowance after routes, helpers and ownership terms: 5545878 and 5563734, each below 10^7.

This starts from the exact source graph used by PR5830. Its cheapest word has peak 65537 and scalar allowance 200546; lowering the peak costs more. Exact rational norms and conserved integer duals prove the full tradeoff at all 16 caps 2^b, plus the sharp original-budget threshold. The default checker needs no solver.

The emitted words have 27102 and 27107 instructions. All 769 entry and 769 exit conversions are charged in each. Four large exit scales are lowered into legal factors with the same total charge. The original coefficient limit and the explicit source operation bound remain intact. Every scalar/native representation invariant, actual emitted-prefix norm, all 782 input axes and 611524 reverse coefficients pass. Literal rows attain the reported peaks. False prices, negative multipliers and an unsupported lower cap reject.

Registered normal/-O, committed-byte and export checks pass. A sealed, read-only, empty-PATH Git-free replay passes in 15.21 seconds without byte or mode changes. The optional NetworkX 3.5 candidate search is separate from acceptance.

This is an ideal amplification construction under the retained unitary native-chart and exact-reset premises. It is not a rounded-child error theorem or a new kappa. Actual error pricing, physical reset/tape admission and full global/compiler hashes remain open. Five framework assumptions remain. Hosted CI and independent admission are separate.

Retain PR5830/5824/5822/5812 and the complete P104 attribution in NOTICE, plus the prior norm/precision context from PR5819 and PR2878. New source-bound frontier and words by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents.
